reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports the first three premises for laser-clad coatings at 900°C, but provides no data on bulk cast material, room-temperature creep, strength/ductility retention, or the proposed segregation/oxide-adhesion mechanism, leaving the last two premises and the mechanistic claim unsupported.
premises: Y and Hf co-doping does not alter the solidification microstructure or phase structure of AlCoCrFeNi2.1
Y and Hf co-doping improves thermal stability (reduces grain coarsening) during high-temperature exposure
Y and Hf co-doping improves hot corrosion resistance (reduces oxide scale spallation) in molten salt
The benefits are achievable in bulk cast material, not just laser-clad coatings
The improvements in thermal stability and corrosion resistance occur without sacrificing strength and ductility
